finding: Measured aerosol emission from three simulated high-risk procedures found that dropping a container of bacterial suspension produced the highest source intensity of the three, with a mean culturable concentration of roughly 10^3 CFU/m^3, above that produced by spillage.
source_title: Three experimental common high-risk procedures: emission characteristics identification and source intensity estimation in biosafety laboratory

finding: Air and surface sampling during centrifugation of blood spiked with a model bacterium recovered no organisms. The centrifugation was performed with closed-cap tubes in a swing-bucket rotor, and the air sampling method had a detection limit of 4 CFU/m^3.
source_title: Aerosol production during blood and urine pre-analytical processing and handling in a hospital biochemistry clinical laboratory during the COVID-19 pandemic

finding: A review of accidental aerosol generation in laboratories includes centrifuge spills among the accident types that have been studied, and centrifuge mishaps appear in the record of incidents associated with laboratory-acquired infection.
source_title: A review of accidental aerosol generation in laboratories and laboratory-associated infections

finding: Measured source intensities for three simulated high-risk procedures place centrifugal tube rupture at roughly 10-100 CFU/m^3, BELOW the roughly 10^3-10^4 CFU/m^3 measured for dropped containers and for accidental injection.
direction: positive, failure mode, but lower than other accident types
source_title: Three experimental common high-risk procedures: emission characteristics identification and source intensity estimation in biosafety laboratory

finding: Air and surface sampling during opening of blood sample tubes spiked with a model bacterium recovered no organisms. The tubes were opened behind a plexiglass panel, and the air sampling method had a detection limit of 4 CFU/m^3.
source_title: Aerosol production during blood and urine pre-analytical processing and handling in a hospital biochemistry clinical laboratory during the COVID-19 pandemic

step_name: Automated clinical chemistry and haematology analyser operation
finding: A review of measured laboratory aerosol generation identifies automated laboratory equipment as a source requiring characterisation, noting that studies have concentrated on manual procedures and accidents.
source_title: A review of accidental aerosol generation in laboratories and laboratory-associated infections

finding: Viable bioaerosol was measured during each stage of the assay workflow. Neither sample preparation nor automated cartridge processing produced any culturable bioaerosols, against measured concentrations of 16 CFU/m^3 and 325 CFU/m^3 generated during preparation of smears for acid-fast microscopy. Benchtop use of the assay limits infection risk to the user.
source_title: Containment of bioaerosol infection risk by the Xpert MTB/RIF assay and its applicability to point-of-care settings

finding: In an investigation of Brucella exposure risk events across ten clinical laboratories, this identification technology was in use during four of the events, and those four events accounted for 84 percent of all personnel exposures identified across the investigation.
source_title: Brucella exposure risk events in 10 clinical laboratories, New York City, USA, 2015 to 2017

finding: In three of the four events involving this technology, the initial Gram stain appearance was of Gram-positive rods or cocci suggestive of streptococci, rather than the small Gram-negative coccobacilli conventionally taught as the cue for a possible biological threat agent.
direction: positive, defines the real failure mode
source_title: Brucella exposure risk events in 10 clinical laboratories, New York City, USA, 2015 to 2017

finding: In the events in which a biological safety cabinet was in use for the manipulations concerned, no seroconversions were identified among the exposed personnel.
source_title: Brucella exposure risk events in 10 clinical laboratories, New York City, USA, 2015 to 2017

finding: Guidance states that commercial identification systems, including this one, should not be used for identification of potential select agents, and that manipulation of organisms that might be Brucella should occur in a cabinet under enhanced practices until ruled out and referred.
source_title: Sentinel level clinical laboratory guidelines for suspected agents of bioterrorism and emerging infectious diseases: Brucella species

finding: In an investigation of laboratory-acquired meningococcal disease, nearly all affected microbiologists had manipulated isolates and performed subplating with a loop on an open bench, and aspiration from blood culture bottles was performed at the open bench without a cabinet, eye protection or a mask.

Sixteen cases of probable laboratory-acquired meningococcal disease were identified, of which eight were fatal. In fifteen of the sixteen laboratories, the isolate had been manipulated outside a biological safety cabinet.
source_title: Assessing the risk of laboratory-acquired meningococcal disease

finding: The estimated attack rate among microbiologists was 13 cases per 100,000 microbiologists, against 0.2 cases per 100,000 among adults in the general population: an occupational rate roughly sixty-five times the background rate.
source_title: Assessing the risk of laboratory-acquired meningococcal disease

finding: Exposure to droplets or aerosols during manipulation of invasive isolates on an open bench top was concluded to be the most likely risk factor.
source_title: Assessing the risk of laboratory-acquired meningococcal disease

finding: In a fatal laboratory-acquired case, the investigation identified multiple breaches, among them manipulation of isolates on the open bench, plate spreading on the open bench, and flaming a slide that had not fully air dried.
source_title: Fatal meningococcal disease in a laboratory worker - California, 2012

finding: Across the Brucella exposure risk events investigated in ten clinical laboratories, open-bench manipulation of isolates gave rise to more than 200 occupational exposures requiring assessment and follow-up.
source_title: Brucella exposure risk events in 10 clinical laboratories, New York City, USA, 2015 to 2017

finding: Guidance records clinical laboratory cases arising from smelling bacteriological cultures and from working on open bench tops.
source_title: Biosafety in microbiological and biomedical laboratories, 6th edition
